Fun Facts

  • This Station, coupled with Blue Swamp Station, alludes to the word Vicissitudes in Chinese.
  • While Blue Swamp Station has water above the ceiling of the platforms and the concourse so that the concourse and the platform are visible with each other, this station has water on the floor in the middle of the Platform, as well as a skylight above the platform.

Line Characteristics and Fun Facts

Main Line (Urban Line)

  • One of the six initially planned lines of NR Los Sengas Division.
  • This line runs entirely at the North-South orientation.
  • Except for the section between and , which runs parallel with , the average interstation distance is longer than other Standard Railway Lines.
  • Most of the section between and shares structure with Route 1.
  • An emergency platform is set up between and . While there were originally plans to set up a station there, this plan was ultimately scrapped.
  • Thie line passes through the most bridges among all Standard Railway Lines. (4 Bridges)
  • This line separates East Los Sengas from West Los Sengas. Areas to the east of are East Los Sengas, whereas areas to the west of are West Los Sengas.
  • The tunnel between Upper Rover Bridge and is also the first Dual Carriageway Tunnel in Los Sengas Division.
  • This line provides Express Services for the following lines:
  • : to . It skips Metro Spring Station and Cyan Loop Station, making the journey more direct.
  • : to . It skips Minstrel Woods Station and makes the journey more direct.
  • While Seraphynx Station was not originally designed to be an station, when considering the fact that passengers to and from and would have to travel down to Mei Fwong Station before connecting to other lines, it was ultimately decided that would stop at Seraphynx Station.While Old Brightland Station also features , and an interchange with of Nawis Railway (NAR), takes very long detours before reaching , and does not share entry gate areas with Standard Railway Lines, meaning that passengers have to take long walks before reaching , not to mention that the NAR Station is not connected to the Nazca Railway Station, meaning that passngers have to take long walks travelling between the stations of the two lines.</ref>

Express Line (Urban Express)

  • While this line is not a Veloduct, as the concept of Veloducts did not appear at the time of this line's establishment, it uses announcements in the style of Veloducts. However, as a result, , which will be established in the future, is not considered to be a part of the Veloducts either.
  • This line became the basis of Veloducts in the future.
  • Thie line was formerly the line which have not completed development and had the longest timespan without any development. (This line had not seen any development for three years and one month, from the completion of Rover Down Checkpoint on August 10 2015 until the completion of Intus Aquilo Gateway in S3E2 on September 21 2018). However, this record was broken in 2020 by on October 2020. At the time, did not have any development for three years and ten months.

title: V-Stock
safeHtml:
The '''V-stock''' is a train designed by "New Horizons Technology" (The parent company of Nazca Railway) designed for Veloduct use based on the N-Stock.

Technical Information

Exterior and Outlook

  • '''Driver Cab Car Length''': 25000 mm
  • '''Normal Car Length''': 22000 mm
  • '''Width''': 3000 mm
  • '''Height''': 3750 mm
  • '''Total Length''' (9-Carriage): 204000 mm (204 m)
  • '''Track Gauge''': 1432 mm
  • '''Car Doors''': 3 doors on both sides for all carriages except the third and the seventh carriages. 5 doors on both sides for the third and the seventh carriages
  • '''Material''': Titanium Alloy
  • '''Destination Indication''': Full-Color LED, alternating between Route Name and Destination Name.

Variants

Code: D－Driver Cab, H－Control Car, M－Motor, P－Pantograph, T－Trailer

DV1xx - PV2xx - '''MV3xx''' - HV4xx - MV5xx - HV6xx - '''MV7xx''' - PV8xx - DV9xx

  • '''9-Carriage''': 5M4T (D-P-M-H-M-T(H)-M-P-D)

After the 100th Rolling Stock: <br />D91xxx - P92xxx - M93xxx - H94xxx - M95xxx - H96xxx - M97xxx - P98xxx - D99xxx

xx and xxx represents the order of rolling stock constructed.

'''Bold''' represents carriages with 5 doors, others represent carriages with 3 doors.

Specifications

This train uses the same components as the N-Stock, but has different maximum speeds.

  • '''Designed Maximum Speed''': 145 km/h
  • '''Operational Maximum Speed''' (Los Sengas): 135 km/h
  • '''Acceleration''': 4.5 km/h/s
  • '''Deceleration''': 2-5 km/h/s

Power Systems

  • '''Electrification''': 1500 V DC (Can be customized for support of 25000V 60Hz AC and alternation between AC and DC).
  • '''Current Collector''': Wireless Pantograph
  • '''Braking system''': Regenerative Braking blended with air brake.

Vehicle Design

Seats

All seats except for in the third and seventh carriages are horizontal seats that automatically changes direction upon reaching the destination. Alternatively, the orientation of the seats can also be manually configured. All seats feature headrests and artificial leateher. Seats in the third and seventh carriages are vertical seats featuring headrests and artificial leather.

Train Interior

Circular Plastic Rings and cylindrical handrails are set up between train doors, with an improved holding position for optimized touch. While there was formerly a hand rail in the middle of the car doors, as it affects the efficiency of passenger flow, they were later removed. To the left of every third door of the third and seventh carriages, a wheelchair space that can put up to two wheelchairs is also available to the left of the third door.

Passenger Information Display System

A 17.5-inch LCD screen is placed on the car door to play advertisements and news information, and two connected 17.5-inch display screens display train information, including the next station, the destination, the station layout and transfer information. In total, there are three 17.5-inch displays on the car door. However, for the V-Stock, another 17.5-inch display is set up perpendicular to the car door so that passengers on horizontal seats can view passenger information.

Car Doors

Car doors are 1500mm wide at 5-door carriages and 1300mm wide at 3-door carriages. All car doors are electrically operated. While the doors are quiet during operation, a sound indicatior will also sound when the doors are about to close to ensure passenger safety.

Neutral Zone

When trains pass through Neutral Zones, the Electrical Voltage becomes Zero, and a loud bang will be heard due to air pressure. However, they only exist in , and other areas are separated using insulators. Signs also exist to indicate the beginning and end of Neutral Zones.

Fun Facts

While this train is mechanically identical to the N-Stock, the facilities in each carriage are modified to fit the needs of Commuter Travel. However, the third and seventh carriages of the V-Stock are identical to that of the N-Stock.

Application

  • All Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division) Veloducts

This rolling stock is only used in the Veloduct as passenger capacity is lower. Therefore, during rush hour, the N-Stock is also used to facilitate passenger flow.

All V-Stock trains support up to nine carriages.

Related Trains

  • N-Stock: The base variant of this train.

Fun Facts

  • The design and layout of this station is similar to Aest Station with regards that both stations have an outdoors structure that is surrounded by two disconnected platforms. However, there are several differences between this station and Aest Station as follows:
  • Most of the Outdoor Space at Aest Station is not covered, whereas a cover is built above the station structure of this Station. This ensure that passengers in the station would not get wet even under rainy weather.
  • While Aest Station has an indoor space beneath the platforms, this Station does not have any indoor spaces except for the platforms.
  • As the two platforms at are separated by tracks, with its tracks closer to the Station Park than the Platforms, that station is seen as having Side Platforms. However, the platforms in this station are linked by Connecting Passageways as the Platforms are closer to the Open Area than the Tracks in this Station. Therefore, this Station is seen as having a Separated Island Platforms.
  • This is the eighth Nazca Railway Station in which the Name of this Station shares the name of the District that houses the station itself, with the first seven being , , , , , Centopia and .

title: Vector Bay Depot
safeHtml:
'''Vector Bay Depot''' is one of the depots of Nazca Railway Los Sengas Division, and it began services on November 2 2016. This Depot provides services for , , , , , , , , , , , , , and , as well as maintenance services for , and trains. This Depot Spans the Kaling Channel, Incident Bay and Vector Bay areas of Downtown, and trains can perform maintenance works in this depot. This depot was formerly the largest depot in Nazca Railway, but was later taken over by the Centopia Depot on July 8 2020. However, this depot once again became the largest depot in terms of Capacity on August 23 when it expanded to provide spaces for 60 additional 9-Carriage Trains in response to the extension to Metropolis Terminal.
